test_title: PYST 3: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 26 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The rare manuscripts had been preserved meticulously by the archivists before the fire broke out.

options.text: The archivists have preserved the rare manuscripts meticulously before the fire broke out.
The archivists preserved the rare manuscripts meticulously before the fire broke out.
The archivists had preserved the rare manuscripts meticulously before the fire broke out.
The archivists has preserved the rare manuscripts meticulously before the fire broke out.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The agent (the archivists) performing the action in the passive sentence becomes the subject of the active sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the sentence is: "The rare manuscripts had been preserved meticulously by the archivists before the fire broke out."
 
• The tense used here is **Past Perfect** (had been preserved).
 
• To convert to active voice: Place the agent "The archivists" at the beginning as the new subject.
 
• Change the passive verb form "had been preserved" to the active form "had preserved" (Structure: *Subject + had + V3 + Object*).
 
• Ensure the adverb "meticulously" and the time clause "before the fire broke out" remain in their logical positions.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The archivists had preserved the rare manuscripts meticulously before the fire broke out."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"The archivists have preserved..." – Incorrect tense (Present Perfect).
 
• **Option 2: **"The archivists preserved..." – Incorrect tense (Simple Past).
 
• **Option 4: **"The archivists has preserved..." – Grammatically incorrect subject-verb agreement and incorrect tense.
